defects: Restricts to LinearIsometryEquiv (a bijective self-map f : E ≃ₗᵢ[𝕜] E) instead of a general linear isometry f : U →ₗᵢ[𝕜] V between possibly distinct spaces U, V — domain and codomain are forced to be equal and the map forced to be invertible, which is a much narrower class of maps than the gold statement covers

Uses ordinary LinearMap.det (only defined for endomorphisms) instead of the gold's LinearMap.normDet, the generalized orthonormal-basis determinant defined for linear maps between possibly different (and possibly differently-dimensioned) inner product spaces — this loses the whole point of the gold theorem (it applies even when domain ≠ codomain)

Drops the third ambient space W present in gold's variable context and collapses U, V into a single space E, losing the generality that only the domain need be finite-dimensional while codomain(s) need not be

Typeclass hypotheses are inconsistent/likely fail to elaborate: [InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E] requires an [RCLike 𝕜] instance, but the statement only provides [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]; likewise InnerProductSpace requires [NormedAddCommGroup E] but only [SeminormedAddCommGroup E] is given
States conclusion as ‖LinearMap.det ...‖ = 1 rather than the gold's f.toLinearMap.normDet = 1, changing which defined quantity is being asserted equal to 1
